title: Sequence Detective Lens — compact trace sifting UI for request drilldowns
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable trace drilldown component (Sequence Detective Lens) that surfaces the most relevant spans, correlation IDs, and anomalous timing without forcing users into a full-page waterfall. This lens will be used inside the Console request list, the per-route dashboard, and a compact floating inspector during rollouts. It must be readable at a glance, support fast filtering by correlation ID and span attributes, and allow lightweight context expansion (peek into full span details).

Motivation: Platform customers need a faster way to triage noisy services and flaky requests. Full waterfall views are powerful but expensive to load. The lens should keep latency low, reveal cost/latency hotspots, and provide direct links to full trace playback or the request forensics workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Lens renders within 200ms when embedded in a route dashboard (mock data acceptable for prototype)
Shows top 6 spans by self-time with visual relative width bars and explicit duration values
Supports search by correlation ID and quick filter chips (error, cold-start, cache-miss)
Clicking a span opens a flyout with full metadata (keys: span_id, parent_id, service, op, start, duration, tags)
Provides an action row: jump-to-full-trace, open-request, create-issue (pre-populated with trace link)
Compact mode collapses details to a single-line summary per request for dense lists
comments: 2025-02-19 — Maya Chen: Initial concept sketched after reviewing ops tickets for noisy endpoints. Attached rough sketches and a comparison matrix against full waterfall and compact timeline patterns.
2025-02-22 — Arjun Patel: Created high-fidelity frames for list-embedded and floating inspector variants. Implemented accessible color tokens and 3 density modes.
2025-02-25 — Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed scope with SRE — prioritized error and latency filters for beta. Requested inclusion of 'cost delta' micro-metric for each request if available.

2025-02-27 — Rafael Gomez (Eng lead): Flagged backend requirement: expose aggregated span self-time and a precomputed top-spans array in the request summary API to avoid fetching full trace on initial render.

2025-03-01 — UX Research (Elena Park): Summary of 6 quick tests with platform engineers: participants preferred the single-line density with inline sparkbars; needed clearer affordance for opening full trace playback.
2025-03-03 — Design critique notes: Reduce decorative separators, increase hit area for filter chips, add micro-animations for span expansion to signal async fetches.
decisions: Ship compact-embedded variant first (route dashboard + request list) and hold floating inspector for follow-up after perf validation.
Expose only top-6 spans by default; allow 'Show all' to request full-list (keeps initial render cheap).
Use the existing rollouts action menu schema so create-issue and open-request actions are consistent with other console components.
risks: If backend does not provide pre-aggregated top spans, initial render may require many backend calls and increase latency.
Overloading the compact view with too many micro-metrics could reduce scan-ability; must balance density vs. clarity.
engineering_notes: Needs new lightweight request-summary API field: top_spans: [{span_id,duration,self_time,op,service,error_flag}]
Suggested payload should be capped to 6-8 spans. If not available, implement a server-side projection in ENG-40212
Front-end: implement optimistic placeholder rows and skeletons; animate height when flyout loads to avoid layout jank
Accessibility: ensure each span row has aria-expanded and aria-controls for flyout content
feedback: From SRE (Jamal Reeves): prefer explicit 'sampled' badge when trace is partial to avoid chasing incomplete traces
From Support (Lina Xu): quick copy button for correlation ID is essential when sharing links in tickets
From Sales (Tom Rivera): include a subtle cost delta indicator to help customers justify adoption of dedup/caching features
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi frames incorporating critique changes (due 2025-03-07)
Align with backend on request-summary schema (ENG sync 2025-03-06)
Prepare A/B prototype for 10 internal users to validate scan-ability vs. full waterfall (UX Research)
